record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Tame-field analogues for perfect henselian fields
record.original_question: Can one prove for henselian perfect valued fields of positive characteristic model-theoretic results analogous to the existing theorems for tame fields, perhaps after imposing only mild additional hypotheses? This question is motivated by the positive result that F_p(t^{1/p^∞})^h is an elementary substructure of F_p((t))^{1/p^∞}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $(K,v)$ be a valued field with value group $vK$ and residue field $Kv$. Recall:

- $(K,v)$ is henselian if $v$ extends uniquely to every algebraic extension of $K$; equivalently, Hensel's lemma holds.
- $(K,v)$ is perfect if $K$ is a perfect field, i.e., $\mathrm{char}(K)=0$ or $\mathrm{char}(K)=p>0$ and the Frobenius $x\mapsto x^p$ is surjective on $K$.
- $(K,v)$ of residue characteristic $p>0$ is called tame if it is henselian, the value group $vK$ is $p$-divisible, the residue field $Kv$ is perfect, and every finite extension $(L|K,v)$ is defectless (i.e., $[L:K]=(vL:vK)\cdot[Lv:Kv]$).
- For a valued field $(K,v)$, $K^h$ denotes its henselization, and $K^{1/p^\infty}=\bigcup_{n\ge 0} K^{1/p^n}$ its perfect hull (in characteristic $p$).

The model theory of tame valued fields is well developed: in particular, the Ax–Kochen/Ershov style Theorem of F.-V. Kuhlmann states that if $(K_1,v_1)$ and $(K_2,v_2)$ are tame valued fields, then $(K_1,v_1)\equiv(K_2,v_2)$ as valued fields if and only if $v_1K_1\equiv v_2K_2$ as ordered abelian groups and $K_1v_1\equiv K_2v_2$ as fields; analogous relative completeness, model completeness, and Ax–Kochen–Ershov principles for elementary equivalence and substructure relations are known in the tame setting.

There is a positive instance suggesting an extension of such results outside the tame realm: for any prime $p$, equipped with the natural $t$-adic valuation, the henselization $\mathbb{F}_p(t^{1/p^\infty})^h$ is an elementary substructure of the perfect hull $\mathbb{F}_p(\!(t)\!)^{1/p^\infty}$ of the Laurent series field. Note that these fields are perfect and henselian but are not tame in general (they may carry nontrivial defect).

Problem. Develop a model theory of henselian perfect valued fields of positive residue characteristic that parallels the model theory of tame valued fields. Concretely, identify mild additional hypotheses $(\ast)$ on a class $\mathcal{C}$ of henselian perfect valued fields of positive characteristic (containing examples such as $\mathbb{F}_p(t^{1/p^\infty})^h$ and $\mathbb{F}_p(\!(t)\!)^{1/p^\infty}$) under which one can prove an Ax–Kochen–Ershov style theorem for $\mathcal{C}$: namely, for $(K_1,v_1),(K_2,v_2)\in\mathcal{C}$,
$$(K_1,v_1)\equiv(K_2,v_2)\iff v_1K_1\equiv v_2K_2\ \text{and}\ K_1v_1\equiv K_2v_2,$$
together with corresponding relative model-completeness and elementary-substructure transfer results.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in a 2025 survey on the model theory of tame valued fields, motivated by a recent result of Jahnke–Kartas establishing one elementary-substructure instance. No general Ax–Kochen–Ershov theorem for henselian perfect valued fields of positive characteristic (beyond the tame case) appears in the literature, and the problem is presented as open as of late 2025.

status_evidence.title: Jahnke–Kartas, Beyond the Fontaine–Wintenberger theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Corollary 1.7.5 establishes that F_p(t^{1/p^\infty})^h is an elementary substructure of F_p((t))^{1/p^\infty}.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the only known positive instance motivating the open problem; no general theory is established.
